Agent Building Handbook: Documentation Plan

Prepared by Prabhat Singh · 27 October 2026 · For stakeholder approval

SECTION 01 OF 11

Summary

Approve this plan to publish the engineering handbook's guidance inside the existing Agent Platform docs. No separate guide section is needed. Each piece of content goes where users do that task, so they meet it early.

  • 9 new pages, each placed in an existing nav group.
  • 2 existing pages absorb larger sections: Test agents becomes Test and debug agents, and Deploy agents gains the release process.
  • About 30 existing pages gain specific facts: defaults, limits, setting paths, and silent failures.
  • Build splits into 7 subgroups so the design pages sit in front of the reference pages.
  • No URL changes and no redirects.

Implementation starts after approval. Engineering must confirm the facts listed under Open questions first.

SECTION 02 OF 11

Scope and sources

Item Detail
Source Building and operating AI agents, the internal FDE handbook, October 2026. About 23,400 words: 11 chapters, a quick reference, and an Arch MCP appendix. Uses a fictional running example, Voyager Airlines.
Target Agent Platform docs at docs.kore.ai/agent-platform, from the docs-v2 repo (branch agentplatform-dev).
Related work ABL how-to guides: 28 published, topics 4 to 25 planned in drafts/abl-howtos-docs/topics.md.
Out of scope Agent Platform v1 docs, API reference pages, and screenshots.

SECTION 03 OF 11

Placement rules

  1. A fact goes on the reference page that owns the setting or construct.
  2. Practice guidance goes on a design page in the same nav group, placed before the reference.
  3. New pages link to the ABL how-to guides instead of repeating them.
  4. Silent failures appear twice: as a Note on the owning page and in one lookup table.
  5. Don't publish internal package version pins, FDE team process, or measured Voyager timings presented as benchmarks.

Plan an agent

  1. Gather journey evidence: what people ask, what the system can do, what must hold. Mark assumptions as questions.
  2. Write scenarios with the six-field table and a short sample dialogue.
  3. Plan journeys that use files: list_attachments, get_attachment, and why a missing extraction proves nothing.
  4. Set measurable targets: completion, correctness, safety, efficiency, recovery.
  5. Budget each turn with the design-choice cost table.
  6. Sort scenarios into risk tiers: read, change, high impact, out of scope.
  7. Plan the test set and scenario portfolio. Link to Design agents and Evaluations.

Collaborate on a project

  1. Choose a working pattern: shared project, project per branch, or integration project plus a CI-only project.
  2. Roles and the project:git permission.
  3. Review through Git: Push to Remote, pull request, Pull from Remote after merge, abl.lock.
  4. Hand off a feature branch, step by step.
  5. Resolve a save conflict.
  6. Team working agreement.

Design agents

  1. Start with one agent. Link to how-tos 1.1, 1.2, and 1.5.
  2. Choose the building block: agent with tools, single tool, specialist, or workflow.
  3. Put each rule where it is enforced: the rule placement table.
  4. Enforce confirmations in the tool.
  5. Design tool contracts for reads and writes, with idempotency. Link to the ABL Tools reference.
  6. Worked example: a cancellation flow from gather to proof.
  7. Keep a large project manageable: agent maps and when to split. Link to how-to 1.9.

Multilingual agents

Takes over the Multi-language support section of Create agents, which keeps a short pointer.

  1. Set the language policy and owners.
  2. Choose the interaction language: language_policy and SET_INTERACTION_LANGUAGE.
  3. Translate stable text: locale assets, {{locale.KEY}}, fallback chain.
  4. Answer from knowledge in each language.
  5. Test the whole conversation in each language. Link to General settings › Localization.

Design voice conversations

Setup steps stay on Voice channels. This page holds the design guidance.

  1. Write for voice: what each channel can show.
  2. Choose Pipeline Voice or Realtime LLM Voice, and the orchestration mode.
  3. Keep one agent and add a phone behavior profile.
  4. Write a voice script and run the script checks.
  5. Handle recognition errors: the input risk table and SECURE_INPUT.
  6. Set listening time per question: turn types and precedence.
  7. Shape spoken output: VOICE PLAIN_TEXT and the platform's spoken-style rules.
  8. Handle interruptions, silence, and recovery.
  9. Plan transfers, outbound calls, and follow-ups.

Test voice agents

  1. Measure what callers hear: voice_dead_air, fillers, the low-latency profile.
  2. Build a voice test matrix.
  3. Turn failures into regression cases.
  4. Choose where to run each test.
  5. Check each test call.
  6. Diagnose a failed call.

Common pitfalls and limits

The 14 silent-failure rows and 7 key limits from the quick reference. Each row links to the page that carries the matching Note. A short intro asks readers to record the configuration used in each test.

Work with a coding assistant

  1. Choose Studio, Arch, or a coding assistant.
  2. Know what the assistant does and what you decide.
  3. Give the assistant context: project map, evidence, constraints, acceptance, checks. Skills, house standards, and AGENTS.md.
  4. Build a customer skill.
  5. Write a request and set limits on actions and data. Templates: orientation, small change, debugging, verification.
  6. Use task modes and match each question to its evidence.
  7. Review the assistant's work: common mistakes and what it may do on its own.
  8. Keep session notes between sessions.

Arch MCP tools and skills

  1. Tool groups, with the live manifest as the current catalog.
  2. The 13 guidance skills.
  3. How guarded edits work.
  4. Where to find each task in Studio and in Arch MCP.

SECTION 08 OF 11

Expanded pages

Test and debug agents (testing)

Rename the sidebar title. Keep the existing sections and add these H2s after Pre-ship checklist. About 2,600 words after the change.

  1. Read what the model received: the Request view, its three parts, and cut markers.
  2. Find the cause: transcript vs trace. Write the cause before the fix.
  3. Layers and where the fix lives: the 8-layer table.
  4. Debug a missing value: five steps and the cut-marker table.
  5. Plan and validate a small change. Test runs write real rows, so read back before retrying a write.
  6. Write a change note: the template, and restore vs rollback.
  7. Review a change: review order and review depth by change type.

Deploy agents (deployment)

Add these H2s after Deployment status. About 3,000 words after the change.

  1. Which version a conversation runs: the caller table and the Deployment Binding check.
  2. Approvals and access: governance policy, Record Qualification, and Arch MCP acting as the signed-in person.
  3. Release an agent to production: test, publish, staging, eval gate, qualify, release, watch.
  4. Before-release checklist: 11 items.

Roll back a deployment gains the restore vs rollback note.

Get started and Build

Handbook section Target page › section Action Content

Creating a project Create and manage project › Import project Expand Import formats: .zip, .agent-bundle.json, .ablenc, .abl, .yaml.

Workflow tool settings Workflows › Attach workflows to agents Expand Sync vs async. timeout_ms up to 300,000, default wait 60 s. Version pinned at deploy. Human Task needs async. Business result vs tool error.
Tool contracts and settings ABL reference › Tools; Tools overview Expand Confirmation question format. A tool with no effect counts as a write. Valid confirm values. process.before never on runtime inputs. ON_ERROR subtypes. timeout vs timeout_ms. store_result.
Prompt Library row Prompts library › Use a prompt in agents Add H2 A linked prompt replaces the generated system prompt. Deployed agents need a new version.
When an Agent Table fits Agent Tables › Choose a table scope Add H2 Project, end user, and session scopes. Empty operation set is read only. Tools API writes reach production rows.
Choosing models AI configuration › Model resolution; General settings › Models Expand Enforced vs compatibility mode. Pipeline Model at Default disables the classifier. One model change per eval run.
Where to keep each value; retention Memory and state › Choose where to keep a value; Best practices Add, Expand Storage table. READONLY limits. Session variables go in every call. User memory needs a verified identity. Never store card data, PINs, or passwords.
What the prompt leaves out How a turn is built › What the model doesn't get Add H2 No current date. Unset placeholders reach the model. LIMITATIONS ignored on orchestrators. Changing values break prompt caching.

Rules for model_context Context size, compaction, and budgets Add H3 Six rules.

Several requests in one message Multi-agent orchestration › Points to note Link How-to 3.6 and Multi-intent recognition.
Remote handoff External agent › Handoff or delegation Expand A registry test doesn't prove a live transfer.
Credentials and tokens Integrations settings › Auth profiles › Secrets Expand No secrets in prompt text. Pass tokens through hidden READONLY variables.
